description: Observed crowding on Muni and the literature behind capacity at boarding (failure to board) in the model (shared/beta3/model.ts boardingAvailability). Used to check where the model's capacity constraint binds; nothing here is fitted. Gathered 2026-10-05; items marked UNVERIFIED could not be confirmed against the primary source.

method.ref: Cepeda, M., Cominetti, R., Florian, M. (2006). A frequency-based assignment model for congested transit networks with strict capacity constraints: characterization and computation of equilibria. Transportation Research Part B 40(6):437-459.
key_facts: DOI 10.1016/j.trb.2005.05.006 (verified via Crossref).

Effective frequency on the boarding arc of line a: f_a(v) = mu_a * [1 - ( v_a / (mu_a*K - vt_a + v_a) )^beta] if vt_a < mu_a*K, else epsilon (tiny). mu_a = nominal frequency (veh/time), K = vehicle capacity, so mu_a*K = line capacity per unit time; v_a = boardings at the stop; vt_a = on-board flow on the in-vehicle segment just after the stop (through flow + boardings). So the denominator mu_a*K - vt_a + v_a is the residual capacity left for boarders (capacity minus through riders). UNVERIFIED against the original text: this general form comes from a secondary summary. It is consistent with the origin-stop special case published in Orlando, Degano & Lotito (arXiv 2405.15631), Eq. 34: f(v) = mu*[1-(v/(mu*K))^beta] for 0<=v<mu*K, else epsilon.
epsilon = 1/999, i.e. an effective headway of about 999 when the vehicle is full (per arXiv 2405.15631, 'As in [2]'). This matches Emme's 999.98 headway cap.
beta: arXiv 2405.15631 uses beta = 0.2 in its CCF example. UNVERIFIED whether CCF's own tests used 0.2. Smaller beta penalises boarding well below capacity; larger beta only near capacity.

Solution method: equilibrium found heuristically by minimising a gap function with the method of successive averages (MSA), per the abstract (Universidad Adolfo Ibanez repository: https://pure.uai.cl/en/publications/a-frequency-based-assignment-model-for-congested-transit-networks).

method.ref: Orlando, Degano & Lotito (2024). An analysis of Wardrop equilibrium and social optimum in congested transit networks. arXiv:2405.15631v2.
key_facts: Open-access restatement of the CCF frequency function (Eq. 34), with epsilon = 1/999 and beta = 0.2.
Equilibrium solved with a 'self-regulated' averaging method rather than plain MSA.

method.ref: Emme capacitated transit assignment (Modeller tool inro.emme.transit_assignment.capacitated_transit_assignment), as invoked by tm2py and the CMAP trip-based model. INRO (Bentley) wrote the Python functions.
key_facts: Each outer iteration runs an extended (optimal-strategy) transit assignment. A user-defined 'headway' function then raises the perceived headway @phdwy on segments where boardings exceed available capacity, with flows averaged (MSA) across iterations.

Headway update (calc_adjusted_headway, identical in tm2py and CMAP): available_cap = max(capacity - transit_volume + transit_boardings, 0); new_phdwy = min(999.98, prev_phdwy * min((boardings+1)/(available_cap+1), 1.5)); new_phdwy = max(line.headway, new_phdwy). This is a multiplicative fixed-point update capped at x1.5 per iteration, not a closed-form CCF function.
Capacity for the period = 60 * period_hours * vehicle.total_capacity / headway (tm2py time_period_capacity).

Stopping criteria (dict passed to the tool): max_iterations, relative_difference, percent_segments_over_capacity. tm2py-utils config and CMAP both use 3, 0.01, 0.01; the CMAP code comments '3 changed from 10 for testing'.
Capacity penalty saved for skims: @capacity_penalty = max(@phdwy - @eawt - line.headway, 0) * 0.5 (headway_fraction 0.5). Skimmed as 'CAPPEN' boarding cost.

Older Emme 4 congestion tool (Queensland TMR PTM documentation, https://tau-docs.tmr.qld.gov.au/ptm/docs/PTM%20Assignment/model_assignment/): effective headway = Min[headway / (1 - (boardings/residual capacity)^headway_adj), 999.98]; capacity = 60*vcapt/hdw; solved by MSA. headway_adj must be calibrated and has no published default. This is the CCF form expressed as a headway.
UNVERIFIED: Emme's own default parameter values and its exact convergence definitions are in the proprietary Emme help and could not be checked publicly.

method.ref: tm2py (MTC Travel Model Two, python): CCR and congested transit assignment
key_facts: TransitConfig fields: use_ccr: bool; ccr_stop_criteria: AssignmentStoppingCriteriaConfig(max_iterations, relative_difference, percent_segments_over_capacity); ccr_weights; eawt_weights; congested_transit_assignment: bool; max_ccr_iterations: float = None (declared but never used in the code).

In the tm2py-utils develop config: use_ccr = false, ccr_stop_criteria = (3, 0.01, 0.01), congested_transit_assignment = true. MTC therefore runs Emme's congested assignment (crowding cost only, no hard capacity) rather than CCR.

CcrWeightsConfig defaults: min_seat 1.0, max_seat 1.4, power_seat 2.2, min_stand 1.4, max_stand 1.6, power_stand 3.4. Segment crowding factor = [seated_pax*(min_seat+(max_seat-min_seat)*(V/C)^power_seat) + standing_pax*(min_stand+(max_stand-min_stand)*(V/C)^power_stand)] / V, minus 1 and floored at 0 (the code notes this is the Toronto form).

EawtWeightsConfig defaults (extra added wait time, minutes): constant 0.259625, weight_inverse_headway 1.612019, vcr 0.005274, exit_proportion 0.591765, default_eawt_factor 1. EAWT = c + w1/headway + w2*V/C + w3*(offs through segment / total offs), multiplied by a per-mode eawt_factor (0.4 or 0.2 for rail modes in the config). The code itself says 'Have no idea what source is here'; the CMAP copy labels it EAWT_AM.

Congested (non-CCR) mode: run for AM/PM only; uses tool inro.emme.transit_assignment.congested_transit_assignment with stop criteria normalized_gap 0.25, relative_gap 0.005 and max_iterations 2-3 per global iteration. Peaking factors am 1.219 and pm 1.262 (peak-hour to period) divide the headway so capacity reflects the peak hour.
Iteration 0 (warm start) runs an uncongested assignment; CCR or congested assignment applies from global iteration >= 1.

method.ref: UK DfT TAG unit M3.2 Public Transport Assignment Modelling (May 2024)
key_facts: 3.6.2 names two crowding effects: (i) in-vehicle discomfort, a crowding factor on IVT that affects all riders on board; (ii) extra waiting at the stop when riders cannot board a full vehicle, estimated with queueing theory from the headway and the probability that vehicles are too full. Only some software supports (ii); otherwise it needs a 'scripted' solution.
3.6.3: crowding requires iterative assignment and calibrated curves. Model it only where it significantly affects behaviour; otherwise monitor V/C.

3.6.4 to 3.6.10: code seated capacity, load distribution factor and crush capacity. Curves may be capped at crush (100%) for stability. Table 3 LSE weights run from sit 1.00 / stand 1.43 at 0 pax/m2 to sit 1.54 / stand 2.21 at 6 pax/m2. Very high modelled standing densities indicate a model problem.
3.6.11: apply within-period demand and supply profiles so peak-within-period crowding is represented.

4.4.3: MSA forces stability without guaranteeing convergence. 4.4.4: target %gap <= 0.1%, where %gap = sum D|C^n - C'^(n-1)| / sum D C'^(n-1). 4.4.6: also report passenger-km per service (<1% change for 95% of services), boardings per service, perceived hours, and perceived wait per service when stop-crowding methods are used. Appendix C covers convergence reporting.

method.ref: Practice values for MSA and convergence (synthesis)
key_facts: CCF and Emme capacitated/congested tools use MSA (step 1/k) on flows. The Emme headway update is additionally damped by the x1.5 cap per iteration.

Production stopping values seen: Emme CCR max_iterations 3, relative_difference 0.01, percent_segments_over_capacity 0.01 (MTC, CMAP); Emme congested normalized_gap 0.25, relative_gap 0.005 (MTC); TAG %gap <= 0.1%.

Cube PT crowding in TM2 (Cube branch, http://bayareametro.github.io/travel-model-two/transit-ccr/guide/): dampening factors link 0.4, volume 0.4, wait 0.4; RMSE convergence 0.01; iterations 1 by default.

sfmtaCrowding.source: SFMTA, Percent of daily Muni trips crowded by route and month (APC data; Tableau CSV)
sfmtaCrowding.date: Monthly May 2022 to May 2026 (CSV pulled 2026-10-05). Page metadata says last updated 2023-05-01, but the data runs through May 2026.
sfmtaCrowding.metric: Percentage of trips where vehicles are above (crowding) capacity for 10% or more of the stops, by route, direction and period (AM 6-9, Mid-Day 9-14, School 14-16, PM 16-19, Evening, Night, Owl). Excludes cable car and historic streetcar.

values.Unweighted mean across all route-directi: AM peak 1.3-3.9% (lowest Jul 2025, highest Oct 2025; May 2026 2.5%); PM peak 1.5-2.9%

sfmtaCrowding.notes: This is a share of trips, not a count of riders left behind. Capacity here is SFMTA 'crowding capacity', not crush.

sfmtaCrowding.source: SFMTA Muni Equity Working Group slides, Sept 19 2024 (service standards)
sfmtaCrowding.metric: Three capacity thresholds by standing space per standee: Planning 4.5 sq ft (bus) / 3.7 (rail); Crowding 3.0 (bus) / 2.7 (rail); Crush 1.5 (bus) / 1.8 (rail). Crowding metric: % of trips over crowding capacity; target < 10% of trips crowded in an hour; a trip counts as crowded if over crowding capacity at >= 5% of stops; routes with >= 10% crowded trips are 'most crowded'.
sfmtaCrowding.notes: The stop share conflicts with the transtat definition (10% of stops). Both are quoted.

sfmtaCrowding.source: SFMTA 2017 Bus Fleet Management Plan, Table 2

values.crush: defined as 1.5 sq ft/pax (APTA gross load); no passenger counts given

sfmtaCrowding.notes: Planning load is applied to the average max load over 30-60 minutes.

sfmtaCrowding.source: SFCTA Congestion Management Program 2021 Final Report, Table 4-13 (SFMTA data)
sfmtaCrowding.metric: Percentage of Muni bus trips over capacity, AM/PM peak (old Strategic Plan metric; target <15%, later <13%)
sfmtaCrowding.notes: Pre-pandemic baseline. The current Strategic Plan metric 'Percent of trips above capacity' is listed as 'metric in development' (https://www.sfmta.com/strategic-planning-metrics-service-quality).

values.N Judah 2016: Morning shuttles cut pass-ups 63% (operations staff tracking); each added car = 119 customers; Inner Sunset/Cole Valley riders often could not board

sfmtaCrowding.notes: No recent systemwide pass-up counts found. The Metro Capacity Study (2025) mentions pass-ups only qualitatively.

metroSubway.source: SFMTA Muni Metro Capacity Study Final Report (approved by SFMTA Board 2025-12-02), Table 1
metroSubway.metric: Peak-hour sq ft per passenger by segment (555 sq ft usable per car). Below 5.4 sq ft = over capacity (FTA Core Capacity); below 10.8 = expected to reach capacity within 10 years.
metroSubway.notes: Passengers per car are my arithmetic (555 / sq ft). No 2024 segment is over capacity on average. Other facts: planning capacity 93 pax/LRV car; the study assumes at most 40 trains/hour/direction in the subway; Van Ness is the maximum load point; Metro carried about 117,000 riders per weekday (Sept 2025), about 70% of pre-pandemic; 'Prior to the pandemic, overcrowding was common'; ridership grew about 20% Sept 2024-Sept 2025 and crowding is re-emerging, especially on the N; at today's frequencies overcrowding is forecast in 10-15 years in the subway, Twin Peaks Tunnel, N and J.

metroSubway.source: SFMTA Muni Metro Capacity Study Draft Recommendations Appendix

values.N, L, M subway segments: over capacity in all growth bands at about 1,000-1,999 riders/hour
values.J: over capacity in all bands at under 1,000/hour

metroSubway.source: SFMTA Train Control Upgrade Project, Board subcommittee presentation
metroSubway.metric: Maximum trains per hour on a single track, peak hour

values.needed for good service: 1-2 min headways, about 45 tph, beyond the current ATCS

metroSubway.notes: SFMTA runs a reduced service plan to limit subway congestion. CBTC promises up to 20% more capacity, in service 2028-2034.

metroSubway.source: SFMTA Subway Performance Data (ATCS), Subway Maximum Trains per Hour at Embarcadero EB
metroSubway.date: about 1 year of weekdays ending around 2025-2026; exact window UNVERIFIED
metroSubway.metric: Daily maximum hourly in-service train arrivals, Embarcadero EB
metroSubway.notes: From an earlier extraction in this project's scratchpad. Under 30 trains/hour, so actual peak service is far below the 40 tph assumption.

metroSubway.source: SFMTA blog 'A 21st Century Plan to Grow SF Rail'

values.subway: operates at about 60% of design capacity in peaks

bart.source: BART Transbay Corridor Core Capacity Program

values.peak: >28,000 pax/hour through the tube; 24 tph max per direction; core capacity target 30 ten-car tph
values.space: about 4.7 sq ft/rider at Embarcadero/West Oakland (pre-pandemic)

bart.notes: Post-2023 load factors not found (UNVERIFIED). BART weekday ridership is about 205k (Q2 2026), well below 2019, so the tube is very unlikely to bind today.

ferryVessels.source: Golden Gate Bridge, Highway and Transportation District, ferry fleet history
ferryVessels.notes: Larkspur service uses the Spaulding class and catamarans; the model takes 600 a sailing for Larkspur and 420 for Golden Gate's other routes (transit.ts).

ferryVessels.source: Bay Crossings, 'WETA Welcomes New 445-Passenger Ferry Pyxis' (2019)

values.Pyxis, Vela, Lyra: 445 passengers each, built for the Vallejo route

ferryVessels.notes: Older SF Bay Ferry vessels carry fewer; the model takes 400 a sailing (transit.ts).

recommendations: Use SFMTA crowding-capacity values as a soft 'crowded' threshold, not as hard boarding capacity: bus 51 (40ft) / 81 (60ft), LRV about 93/car (planning) to about 103/car (5.4 sq ft). Make the hard capacity crush or near it (about 1.5 sq ft/standee; roughly 1.2-1.3x crowding capacity) and apply a peak-hour factor (MTC uses 1.219 AM, 1.262 PM) when the period is longer than an hour. Plausibility checks: (1) mid-day, evening and night riders left behind should be about 0 everywhere; (2) in the AM peak, failure-to-board should appear only on the routes with the most crowded trips: 1 California (IB AM, OB PM), 38R, 45, 30X, 5R, 2, 12, 22 and N Judah (IB AM, OB PM; inner Judah about 88 pax/car); on the 28, 29, 24 and 48 it belongs in the school period; (3) even on the worst route only 25-34% of peak trips reach crowding capacity, and the all-route average is about 2-4%, so modelled left-behind should be a small share of route boardings (a few percent at most at the max-load stops), not tens of percent; (4) in the Market Street subway the 2024 peak-hour average is about 65 pax/car at Van Ness against 93 planning, so the subway as a whole should show no or negligible left-behind in 2024-26, with any J/K/L/M left-behind being a red flag; (5) BART and the Transbay Tube should not bind today. If the model leaves riders behind on many routes, check capacity units (per vehicle vs per period), headways and peak-hour factoring before tuning beta or MSA.
